setup: Lie on your back on a mat
Press your lower back into the floor
Arms overhead, legs long and together
execution: Lift your shoulders and legs off the floor
Keep your lower back pinned down
faults: Don't let your lower back arch up

notes: If your lower back lifts off the floor, shorten the lever: bend the knees or bring the arms forward until it stays down.
End the hold when the position breaks rather than pushing on with an arched back.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Tuck hollow hold
regressions.reason: Knees bent toward the chest and arms by the sides; much shorter lever.

regressions.name: Dead bug

progressions.name: Hollow rock

progressions.name: V-up

progressions.name: Toes-to-bar

substitutions.name: Dead bug
substitutions.reason: Easier on the back position; good warm-up.

substitutions.name: Ab-wheel rollout

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at floor level so the gap (or no gap) under the lower back is visible. Mat along the floor line, head on the left.

keyPositions.label: Set
keyPositions.describe: Lying flat, arms resting overhead, legs straight. Lower back pressed into the mat.

keyPositions.label: Hold
keyPositions.describe: Shoulder blades just off the mat, arms by the ears and off the floor, straight legs lifted about 20–30° with feet together. Body forms a shallow banana shape; only the lower back and hips touch the mat.

ikHints: Lower back and pelvis stay in contact with the mat
emphasise: No gap under the lower back
Low, long legs and arms make it harder
doNotShow: Lower back arched off the mat
